## Findings ledger
- [C2.DOC2.F2] The United States answers how it intervened in SeaMeWe-6: it used incentives and threats, including financing, training grants and threatened sanctions, after which the consortium awarded the contract to SubCom — dim: case_answers — case: United States / SeaMeWe-6 — criterion: What mechanism did the case actor use to reshape the cable market, and with what reported consequence? — value-kind: qualitative — evidence-role: reported result — scope: SeaMeWe-6 supplier decision, 2021 — anchor: "Once the threat of sanctions became more concrete, other consortium members were getting second thoughts: factoring in potential sanctions, HMN Tech became an increasingly costly option." — doc: subsea — causal-attribution: United States named by the surrounding attributed account, but the quoted sentence identifies sanctions as the operative pressure — confidence: high — anchor-b: "In late 2021, the consortium held a decisive vote, with a majority opting to award the contract to SubCom." — doc-b: subsea.
- [C2.DOC2.F4] PEACE answers the project-status criterion positively: the cable became operational in 2022, while EMA is separately reported as a project developed following China’s exclusion from SeaMeWe-6; the text does not attribute EMA’s reactive development to PEACE itself — dim: case_answers — case: PEACE cable / EMA cable — criterion: What is the separately stated operational status and chronology of each parallel project? — value-kind: binary — evidence-role: reported result — scope: PEACE cable, 2022; EMA chronology following SeaMeWe-6 exclusion — anchor: "One such effort is the PEACE cable, which be -\ncame operational in 2022." — doc: subsea — causal-attribution: PEACE’s operational status is attributed to PEACE; EMA’s reactive chronology is attributed to China, not PEACE — confidence: high — anchor-b: "Following its exclusion from SeaMeWe- 6, China reportedly began developing another proj -\nect, the Europe- Middle East- Asia (EMA) cable." — doc-b: subsea
- [C2.DOC2.F6] France answers how it sought to retain cable-sector capacity: the state, through APE, agreed to acquire 80% of ASN for €350 million, with the intention of buying the remaining 20% from Nokia after a transition period; the source presents this as an industrial and strategic intervention, not as the same instrument as any other proposal — dim: case_answers — case: France / ASN — criterion: What instrument and mechanism did the case actor use to preserve strategic cable-sector capacity? — value-kind: quantitative — evidence-role: mechanism — scope: ASN ownership and French industrial capacity, November 2024 — anchor: "a deal was struck in November: the French state, via its public holding agency APE" — doc: subsea — causal-attribution: France named by the attributing sentence — confidence: high — anchor-b: "would acquire 80% of ASN for €350 million, with the intention to buy the remaining 20% from Nokia after a transition period" — doc-b: subsea

scope_outcomes.criterion: Retain anchored answers supplied by the source about case actors, instruments, mechanisms, capacities, markets, institutions, consequences and separately attributed project chronology or reactive status.
scope_outcomes.basis: The inspected article supplies anchored case answers for China, the United States, PEACE, EMA and France/ASN, including distinct project chronologies and attributed mechanisms or consequences.
limitations: The comparison is limited to the cases, instruments and outcomes explicitly reported in the supplied article.
PEACE operational status and EMA reported development are distinct findings; the source does not establish causal transfer between them.
No common cross-case quantitative effectiveness denominator is supplied.

evidence_state.coverage_basis: reader/reviewer report; source bytes do not establish inspection or completeness
blocking_issues: Findings lost anchor evidence; this does not establish absence
One or more declared finding references lack retained verified evidence
